## Purpose {#purpose}

JOREK is a nonlinear extended-MHD code with a flux-aligned finite-element grid that
includes the X-point, scrape-off layer and divertor. The Tokamak Toolkit uses it as an
external, open (Tier A) reference for MHD stability, which its transport loop does not
model. It serves brief invariants 1–3: JOREK runs outside JAX, is never called inside
compiled code, and is never a runtime dependency of a surrogate.

## Scope {#scope}

Owner decision [OQ-37](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-37):

| step | what | status |
|---|---|---|
| A | linear pedestal-stability scans over toroidal mode number, ITER hybrid first, then MAST-U | ITER: case (a) closed on the time-step check; case (b) running ([J5](#j5)) |
| B | n = 1 internal-kink check of the sawtooth trigger, same pipeline | after A |
| C | a surrogate of a JOREK quantity behind a guard | decided after A's cost is known |
| D | nonlinear ELM crash runs | reference runs only, later |
| E | disruptions, vertical displacement events, shattered pellet injection | outside the brief; deferred |

Licence: GNU LGPL v3 or later. JOREK is executed as a separate program and is not
vendored, so the toolkit's own licence is unaffected. Results that use JOREK cite the
JOREK overview papers and acknowledge the JOREK team (bottom of this page).

## Build {#build}

JOREK is built from source at a pinned commit; there are no tagged releases. The
build uses GNU Fortran 12.3 and OpenMPI 4.1 with OpenBLAS, ScaLAPACK, FFTW, HDF5,
METIS and ParMETIS. The sparse direct solver is our own MUMPS 5.7.3 build, with PORD,
METIS and ParMETIS orderings. Binaries are compiled for x86-64-v3, so the same binary
runs on the Intel login nodes and the AMD compute nodes. `util/config.sh` fixes the
physics model and toroidal resolution at compile time and edits a source file, so each
configuration is built in its own git worktree.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Build notes

- MUMPS: build the real and complex libraries one after the other. A parallel build
  of both races on Fortran module files.
- GNU Fortran rejects a space between a namelist name and its subscript
  (`name (1) = …`), which Intel Fortran accepts. Upstream inputs are rewritten without
  it; values are unchanged.
- The code's default solver is STRUMPACK. Runs with MUMPS set `use_mumps = .t.` and
  `use_strumpack = .f.` in the namelist.
- `eqdsk2jorek` needs the DIERCKX (FITPACK) spline library, built from netlib with
  double-precision default reals.
- With more than one toroidal harmonic, JOREK needs at least two MPI ranks.
:::

**Regression checks.** These use JOREK's own cases and the reference data the JOREK
team publishes, so the check does not depend on toolkit code ([3 of 4 upstream regression cases reproduce their public reference data: MAST-U grid and equilibrium (largest difference 2.0e-5, tolerance 1e-4), MAST equilibrium with coils (1.2e-10), and one implicit tearing-mode step (4.1e-13, tolerance 1e-12); the full-MHD kink case was not run because its upstream input is out of date for this code version]{.claim}[C-210](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-210){.cid .st-measured}).
On the compute nodes, one job repeated them and measured the step cost
([all three regression cases pass on a 256-core AMD node; one implicit step on the MAST-U X-point grid (8050 elements, toroidal modes n = 0 and 1) takes 5.8 s at 2 ranks x 16 threads, 6.7 s at 4 x 32 and 8.1 s at 2 x 64; the whole job used 22.4 core-hours]{.claim}[C-211](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-211){.cid .st-measured}).

| case | exercises | result |
|---|---|---|
| `grid_with_patches_mastu_303` | MAST-U EQDSK → flux-aligned grid to the wall, fixed-boundary equilibrium | pass |
| `inmast_coils_600` | MAST equilibrium with coils, `model600` | pass |
| `tear_circ_199` | one implicit time step with MUMPS, three harmonics | pass |
| `kink_circ_710` | one time step, full MHD | not run: the upstream input sets a removed parameter and fails a newer consistency check |

## Unit conversion and input files {#adapter}

`tkit.adapters.jorek` (Tier A, host side) converts between SI/eV and JOREK's
normalised units. With $n_0 = \texttt{central\_density}\cdot10^{20}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}$
and $\rho_0 = \texttt{central\_mass}\cdot m_\mathrm{u}\, n_0$:

$$
n = \rho\, n_0,\qquad T_\mathrm{eV} = \frac{T}{e\,\mu_0\, n_0},\qquad
t_\mathrm{SI} = t\,\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0},\qquad \gamma_\mathrm{SI} = \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0}},
$$

using the constants of the pinned JOREK version (`models/constants.f90`), not CODATA.
Single-temperature models evolve $T = T_e + T_i$, with $p = \rho T/\mu_0$. The toroidal
mode number of Fourier component $k$ (1-based) is $\lfloor k/2\rfloor\, n_\mathrm{period}$.

What the adapter covers:

- **Profile files** are two bare numeric columns ($\psi_N$, value). JOREK's reader stops
  silently at the first unparseable line, so the writer emits no header and reads every
  file back for an exact match.
- **Namelists** are written one entry per line, with full precision and no space before
  subscripts. Index ranges such as `fbnd(2:4)` and both quote styles are supported. A
  parser for JOREK inputs is included.
- **Energy reader.** It reads magnetic and kinetic energy per Fourier component from a
  restart file, and checks the array shapes and that the stored time unit matches the
  normalisation.
- **Growth rates** are a least-squares fit of $\tfrac12\ln E$ against time over a
  window the caller must give. No default window is offered, because choosing the
  linear phase is part of the analysis.

**Correctness.**
- The conversion matches the units JOREK stored in three restart files
  ([time and resistivity units computed by the toolkit match the values JOREK stored in three restart files to 1e-15 relative]{.claim}[C-213](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-213){.cid .st-tested}).
- A rewritten MAST-U input gives an identical restart file ([the MAST-U input (356 entries) parsed and rewritten by the toolkit gives, with one thread, a restart file identical in every dataset to a run of the original input]{.claim}[C-214](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-214){.cid .st-measured}).
- The tests are in [26 tests pass in normal and Tier-A-only modes: unit conversion, profile files, namelists, the energy reader, and the runner with fake executables (snapshots, retry, timeout, provenance)]{.claim}[C-215](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-215){.cid .st-tested}.

**Design decisions.**
- *Conversion only, deliberately.* JOREK's own scripts hard-code physics choices: the
  scrape-off-layer extension, diffusivities, resistivity and grid sizes. Here each of
  them is a required input, so it reaches the owner as a decision ([OQ-39](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-39)).
- *Native HDF5, not IMAS output.* JOREK's IDS writer needs the IMAS Fortran access
  layer, and its Python scripts use the pre-2.0 IMAS API.

## Run wrapper {#runner}

`tkit.datasets.jorek_run` runs one case in a new directory:

1. It snapshots the executable and every input read-only, and verifies any input
   provenance.
2. Each attempt gets fresh working copies. The namelist goes on standard input, and
   the launcher sets MPI ranks and OpenMP threads explicitly.
3. The process group is killed at the timeout, and partial output is kept.
4. The outcome is classified: completed, solver aborted, grid set-up abort, JOREK
   error, non-zero exit or timeout.
5. A provenance record is written beside every retained file. `result.json` records
   ranks, threads and whether the run is bitwise repeatable.

Two measured JOREK properties shape it ([an assertion in the element search tree aborts 3 of 8 grid set-up runs at 8 OpenMP threads and 0 of 8 at 1 thread; two 4-thread runs of the same input differ at round-off, while 1-thread runs repeat bit for bit]{.claim}[C-212](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-212){.cid .st-measured}):
- Threaded runs are not bitwise repeatable, so only one-thread runs are marked
  repeatable.
- Threaded runs intermittently abort on an assertion in the element search tree during
  grid set-up, before any time step. The wrapper retries only that case, only before
  the first step, and keeps every attempt.

On the real program the wrapper reproduces a manual run exactly. A completed run is
not physical acceptance.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Post-mortem: a GMRES abort recorded as a completed run (2026-10-24)

- **What was written, and what was correct.** The wrapper classified any run that exited
  with code 0 as completed, unless it had timed out or hit the known grid set-up assertion.
  JOREK stops a run whose iterative linear solver (GMRES) fails to converge, but it exits
  with code 0. The correct classification is a separate outcome,
  `solver_aborted`: the energies up to the abort are valid data, and the run is not
  retried, because a retry would fail the same way.
- **What it looked like from inside.** All eight linear runs of the first case (a) scan
  ended this way and were recorded as `completed` ([8 of 8 case (a) runs ended on the GMRES abort with exit code 0; a test now checks that such a run is recorded as solver_aborted and not retried]{.claim}[C-230](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-230){.cid .st-tested}). Every wrapper
  check passed: the exit code was 0, the output files existed, and the provenance records
  were complete. None of them reads the end of the log.
- **What caught it.** The growth-rate analysis: the energy traces ended at different
  times, and each run's log ended with the abort message. The analysis reads JOREK's own
  output, not the wrapper's status, so it is independent of the classifier.
- **Before and after.** Before: 8 of 8 runs `completed`. After: 8 of 8 `solver_aborted`,
  energies kept.
- **What changed.** The abort string is now an outcome of its own. The test
  `test_gmres_abort_with_exit_zero_is_not_completed` runs a stub JOREK that prints the abort
  and exits 0, and checks that the run is classified `solver_aborted` and is not retried.
- **Blast radius.** None published: no growth rate had been reported from these runs. The
  abort follows the linear phase in every run, so the growth data stay usable.
:::

## ITER hybrid equilibrium {#iter-equilibrium}

Input: the ITER hybrid EQDSK distributed with TORAX (COCOS 2, $I_p$ 11.77 MA,
$B_0$ 5.3 T). A JOREK stability run starts from an equilibrium JOREK solves itself, from
a boundary, a pressure profile and FF′. The acceptance tolerance ([OQ-39](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-39), decision 2) is
q within 2% of the source over $\psi_N$ 0.1–0.95, and $I_p$ within 1%, before any
stability run.

**Current route: fixed boundary on the EQDSK separatrix.** The boundary is the EQDSK
separatrix itself: 300 points on the flux surface $\psi = \psi_\mathrm{bnd}$, ordered by
angle about the geometric centre, with no X-point and a polar flux-aligned grid
(`scripts/jorek/iter_lcfs_input.py`). Pressure and FF′ are those of the first route below.
JOREK `model303` solves the fixed-boundary equilibrium on one core.

| grid ($n_\mathrm{flux}$ × $n_\theta$) | result | accepted |
|---|---|---|
| 40 × 64 | [I_p −1.38%, largest q difference 1.1%: fails the current tolerance]{.claim}[C-220](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-220){.cid .st-measured} | no |
| 80 × 128 | [I_p −0.93%, largest q difference 1.1%, q 4.668 against 4.668 at psi_N 0.95: passes the tolerance of q within 2% and I_p within 1%]{.claim}[C-221](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-221){.cid .st-measured} | yes |
| 160 × 256 | [I_p −0.20%, largest q difference 1.1%: passes]{.claim}[C-222](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-222){.cid .st-measured} | yes |

The largest q difference, 1.1%, is in the core and is the same on all three grids. Edge q
agrees to better than 0.3%. The current deficit shrinks with resolution but is not yet in
a clean asymptotic regime. The 80 × 128 grid is used for the n-scans and 160 × 256 for
the doubled-resolution check.

*Limitation.* A fixed boundary at the separatrix acts as an ideal conducting wall there,
with no vacuum region. Peeling modes, which need one, are artificially stabilised. All
growth rates on this page carry this limitation.

**First route: `eqdsk2jorek` (2026-10-16).** `eqdsk2jorek` produced the boundary, FF′ and
namelist after three changes:
- the spline smoothing was raised from 1e-6 to 3e-5, the smallest value for which the
  fit succeeds; the RMS fit error is about 2e-7 Wb;
- the converter's pressure continuation went to −10 Pa outside the separatrix, because
  the EQDSK pressure there is 0 and the converter's edge value is 10 Pa;
- the temperature file was therefore written by the toolkit: EQDSK pressure inside,
  a 10 Pa floor outside, check-only.

Its result, [JOREK solving the ITER hybrid equilibrium from the TORAX EQDSK matches its safety factor q to 0.4% (median) for normalised flux 0.1-0.5, but is 3.6% high for 0.5-0.9 and 5.8% high for 0.9-0.95 (q 5.12 vs 4.67 at 0.95); plasma current 12.06 vs 11.77 MA]{.claim}[C-216](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-216){.cid .st-superseded} (superseded by [C-221](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-221)), failed the tolerance at the edge.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Post-mortem: the edge mismatch came from the converter's boundary (2026-10-16)

- **What was written, and what was correct.** `eqdsk2jorek` builds a free-boundary-style
  domain from a default ITER contour outside the wall, and takes ψ on that contour from
  the EQDSK. That is correct only if the EQDSK grid covers the contour. The TORAX EQDSK
  comes from a fixed-boundary CHEASE solve: its R–Z grid holds no X-point ($|\nabla\psi|$
  has no zero inside it, and a minimiser leaves the grid), and 187 of the contour's 257
  points lay outside the grid. ψ there was extrapolated, and JOREK built its own X-point and
  separatrix, enclosing a larger plasma than the EQDSK's. The correct boundary for this
  source is its own separatrix.
- **What it looked like from inside.** The converter ran without error once the
  smoothing was raised, the sign conventions all came out right, and core q matched to
  0.4%. Only edge q and the current were off, by a few percent, which entry 65 listed with
  three candidate causes.
- **What caught it.** Checking where the contour points fall relative to the EQDSK grid,
  then solving on the separatrix, which removes the edge mismatch at every resolution.
- **Before and after** (q difference against the EQDSK; $I_p$ against 11.77 MA):

  | route | $\psi_N$ 0.5–0.9, median | $\psi_N$ 0.9–0.95, median | $I_p$ |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | converter contour | +3.6% | +5.8% | +2.5% |
  | EQDSK separatrix, 80 × 128 | +0.2% | +0.1% | −0.93% |

- **What changed.** The EQDSK separatrix is the boundary for every ITER case, and the
  equilibrium is checked against the decision-2 tolerance before any stability run.
- **Blast radius.** Entry 65's claim [C-216](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-216) is marked superseded by [C-221](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-221). It was measured
  correctly for the route it describes, so it is not retracted. No stability result used
  the first route.
:::

## Linear stability scans (J5) {#j5}

### Settings {#j5-settings}

Owner decisions [OQ-39](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-39) (16 Oct) and [OQ-41](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-41) (25 Oct):

| setting | value |
|---|---|
| model | `model303`: reduced MHD with parallel flow, one temperature, diamagnetic terms on |
| dissipation | Spitzer η ($Z_\mathrm{eff}$ 1), temperature-dependent, with the axis value at $T_e = T(0)/2$, because JOREK sets $T_0$ to the axis value of the temperature file; viscosity at Prandtl number 1; parallel viscosity 10×; $D_\perp = \chi_\perp$ = 1 m²/s; Spitzer parallel conduction |
| diamagnetic terms | `tauIC` $= m_i / (2 e F_0 \sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0})$ |
| toroidal modes | n = 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 16, 20, one harmonic per run (`n_tor` 3, `n_period` n) |
| time step, grid | Δt = 1 (JOREK units), 80 × 128; one node, 32 cores per run |
| unstable | γ > 0 with diamagnetic terms; ω* and the EPED-like ratio γ/ω* also reported |
| quotable | only if halving Δt and doubling both resolutions each change γ by at most 5%, with the same location class (decision 7) |

Each job runs an axisymmetric start, then a health gate, then all n in parallel from that
state. The gate requires the minimum of ψ within 1e-3 (relative) of the equilibrium's axis
value, since a deeper minimum signals a blow-up, and positive density and temperature. Two keys that JOREK's own IMAS input script sets
(`eta_coul_log_dep`, `T_min_ZKpar`) don't exist in `model303` and are left out.

**Growth-rate analysis** (`scripts/jorek/j5_growth.py`). γ is the least-squares slope of
½ ln E of the total (magnetic + kinetic) energy over an energy band. A phase counts as
linear only if the two half-windows and the separate magnetic and kinetic fits agree within
2%, over at least 20 points. The band, 1e-15 to 1e-7, was chosen after inspecting the case
(a) traces; the first rule, a steady per-step rate over the final segment, cannot work when
every run ends in a solver abort and some modes exchange energy between the magnetic and
kinetic parts every few steps. Location is the peak of the RMS perturbation over $\psi_N$
bins: axis if the peak is below 0.05, edge at or above 0.8, otherwise core. Since case (b), it is reported from
both the temperature (`class`) and the flow perturbation (`class_u`). ω*ᵢ and γ/ω* are
estimates computed from the profiles, not JOREK outputs.

### Case (a): the EQDSK as given {#case-a-n-scan}

Pressure from the EQDSK, split into density and temperature with TORAX's main-ion density
at 80 s (D-T, mean mass 2.515 amu). The total axis temperature is therefore high
([66.6 keV in case (a) (EQDSK pressure split by TORAX density) against 14.4 keV in case (b) (TORAX at 80 s)]{.claim}[C-239](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-239){.cid .st-measured}): the EQDSK is a higher-pressure state than TORAX at that time, and
diamagnetic stabilisation is overstated.

- **Job 1** (Δt = 3) was lost: its axisymmetric start went numerically unstable, and
  every linear run failed on its first step. The health gate was added after it.
- **Job 2** (Δt = 1) ran 3 h 51 min. Every linear run grew from about 1e-20 over roughly
  16 decades and then stopped on JOREK's GMRES abort ([8 of 8 case (a) runs ended on the GMRES abort with exit code 0; a test now checks that such a run is recorded as solver_aborted and not retried]{.claim}[C-230](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-230){.cid .st-tested}). In this JOREK
  version `linear_run` is `keep_n0_const`: n = 0 is frozen, but the n ≠ 0 equations stay
  nonlinear, so the matrix drifts as the mode grows and the GMRES iteration count rises
  step by step until it fails. Fit consistency: [half-window and magnetic/kinetic fits agree within 1.1% (tolerance 2%) in all 8 runs; moving the energy band one decade either way changes γ by at most 0.6%]{.claim}[C-231](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-231){.cid .st-measured}.

γ is in units of $1/\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0}$, with $\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0}$ = 5.305e-7 s:

| n | γ√(μ₀ρ₀) | γ (s⁻¹) | peak $\psi_N$ | class | γ/ω*_pi,max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.0284 | 5.36e4 | 0.175 | core | — |
| 2 | 0.0126 | 2.38e4 | 0.175 | core | — |
| 3 | 0.0120 | 2.25e4 | 0.175 | core | — |
| 5 | 0.0275 | 5.19e4 | 0.125 | core | — |
| 8 | 0.0281 | 5.30e4 | < 0.02 | axis | — |
| 12 | 0.0440 | 8.29e4 | 0.975 | edge | 0.23 |
| 16 | 0.0374 | 7.06e4 | 0.975 | edge | 0.14 |
| 20 | 0.0330 | 6.22e4 | < 0.02 | axis | — |

Claims: n = 12 [γ√(μ₀ρ₀) 0.0440 (γ 8.3 × 10^4^ s⁻¹), peak at psi_N 0.975, γ/ω* 0.23]{.claim}[C-223](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-223){.cid .st-preliminary}; n = 16 [γ√(μ₀ρ₀) 0.0374 (γ 7.1 × 10^4^ s⁻¹), peak at psi_N 0.975, γ/ω* 0.14]{.claim}[C-224](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-224){.cid .st-preliminary}; core modes
[γ√(μ₀ρ₀) 0.012–0.028, peak at psi_N 0.12–0.18, where q has its minimum of about 1.11]{.claim}[C-225](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-225){.cid .st-preliminary}; axis modes [γ√(μ₀ρ₀) 0.028 and 0.033, confined to psi_N below 0.02]{.claim}[C-226](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-226){.cid .st-preliminary}.

- **Pedestal modes.** Only n = 12 and 16. Their γ/ω* is below the EPED-like ¼, but that
  reading assumes an ideal γ, and these include diamagnetic stabilisation.
- **Core modes.** n = 1–5 peak at $\psi_N$ 0.12–0.18, where the case (a) q profile has its
  minimum: reversed shear, q 2.32 on axis, $q_\mathrm{min}$ ≈ 1.11 at $\psi_N$ 0.15–0.2,
  $q_{95}$ 4.67. Low shear just above q = 1, with the overstated core pressure, favours
  infernal-type core modes.
- **Axis modes.** n = 8 and 20 are confined to $\psi_N$ < 0.02; a high-n mode at the axis is
  probably numerical.
- **Hidden modes.** For these six n, a slower pedestal mode of the same n, if one exists,
  is hidden, because the fastest mode dominates the energy.

### Convergence check {#convergence-check}

The third and last [OQ-39](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-39) job: Δt = 0.5 on 80 × 128 for n = 8, 12, 16, 20, restarting
from job 2's axisymmetric state so that only Δt changes; then the doubled grid, 160 × 256,
for n = 12 and 16, and n = 8 and 20 after the Δt runs. The analysis
(`scripts/jorek/j5_convergence.py`) applies the same band fit to both jobs and requires a
change of at most 5% and the same location class.

| n | class | Δt = 1 → 0.5 | 160 × 256 | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12, 16 | edge | [n = 12: 0.04397 → 0.04397 (−0.01%); n = 16: 0.03744 → 0.03633 (−2.94%); both within the 5% tolerance]{.claim}[C-227](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-227){.cid .st-measured} | not run | converged in Δt; grid not checked |
| 8, 20 | axis | [n = 8: 0.02810 → 0.02967 (+5.56%); n = 20: 0.03300 → 0.03473 (+5.27%); both outside the 5% tolerance]{.claim}[C-228](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-228){.cid .st-measured} | not run | not converged |

All four Δt = 0.5 runs have clean linear phases (spread ≤ 1.5%, band sensitivity ≤ 0.3%),
keep their location, and end on the GMRES abort after it.

The doubled grid never got past its axisymmetric start ([about 126 s per step against 9.7 s on 80 x 128 (13x); timed out after 43 of 50 steps, so no doubled-grid linear run started]{.claim}[C-229](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-229){.cid .st-measured}). Scaling the
step cost by the same factor gives roughly 50–75 s per linear step; the n = 12 and 16 fit
windows need about 700–800 steps, so about 10–17 h at 32 cores. These are estimates, not
measurements; either way a linear run on this grid needs more than one 6 h job.

The job also lost compute to a batch-script bug ([about 290 of 1046 core-h: after the last run ended the script waited on its watchdog (an empty wait list became a bare wait); fixed in both job scripts]{.claim}[C-232](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-232){.cid .st-measured}). The script waited on
its background jobs other than the watchdog, `wait $(jobs -p | grep -v …)`. When that list
was empty, the command became a bare `wait`, which also waits for the watchdog, and the
watchdog never exits. Both J5 job scripts now skip the wait when the list is empty.

*Decision [OQ-41](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-41).* Case (a) is closed on the Δt check: n = 12 and 16 are "converged in Δt,
grid not checked", not quotable; the other six n are "not measured: core or axis mode
faster". The full check moves to case (b), with up to five one-node jobs of ≤ 6 h, each
announced.

### Case (b) equilibrium {#case-b-equilibrium}

Case (b) is the TORAX ITER hybrid state at 80 s: pressure from TORAX's density and
temperatures, FF′ from TORAX's current density with the bootstrap current. The FF′
formula reproduces the EQDSK's own FF′ from the CHEASE geometry to 2.4%.

The first solve gave $I_p$ +3.7% (10.89 against 10.5 MA) and q +7.8% (median, $\psi_N$
0.1–0.5), outside decision 2. The cause is structural: TORAX evolves the current on a fixed
CHEASE geometry, so its state is not a Grad–Shafranov equilibrium, and a consistent
equilibrium with the same p and j has different flux surfaces and q.

*Decision [OQ-40](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-40) (a).* FF′ is multiplied by one factor k so that $I_p$ = 10.5 MA.
Acceptance: $I_p$ within 1%, and p($\psi_N$) as TORAX's by construction. The q difference
from TORAX is reported as a known inconsistency of the fixed-geometry TORAX state.
Rejected: (b) tuning FF′ until q matches, which moves the current profile away from
TORAX's; (c) a self-consistent free-boundary TORAX state first, a larger piece of work.

**Convergence of the Grad–Shafranov iteration.** Without under-relaxation every case (b)
solve stalls ([the iteration cycles between two states for all 200 iterations (axis moves about 5 mm, residual about 7e-3); I_p +3.7% at FF' x 1, −0.0002% at x 0.952, neither converged]{.claim}[C-234](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-234){.cid .st-measured}): the magnetic axis moves between R 6.2986 and 6.3038 m on
alternate iterations. The 2026-10-16 solve already had this (residual 8.2e-3) and it was not
flagged then. Case (b)'s FF′ is hollow, because the ramp-up current has not yet reached the
core, so the axis is weakly pinned. JOREK's `amix` 0.5 ($\psi_\mathrm{new}$ = 0.5
$\psi_\mathrm{old}$ + 0.5 $\psi_\mathrm{solve}$) converges it to 1e-6 in 43 iterations.

| k | `amix` | $I_p$ (MA) | against 10.5 MA | converged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.000 | 0 | 10.887 | +3.7% | no |
| 0.963 | 0 | 10.589 | +0.84% | no |
| 0.952 | 0 | 10.49998 | −0.0002% | no |
| 0.952 | 0.5 | 10.541 | +0.39% | yes |
| **0.947** | **0.5** | **10.501** | **+0.01%** | **yes** |

Accepted: [I_p 10.501 MA against TORAX's 10.5 MA (+0.01%), converged in 43 iterations; on 160 x 256 −0.07% with q equal to about 1e-5]{.claim}[C-233](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-233){.cid .st-measured}. q against TORAX: [median q difference +10.7% (psi_N 0.1–0.5), +3.2% (0.5–0.9), −4.9% (0.9–0.95); q95 4.64 against 4.89, q_min 1.84 against 1.64]{.claim}[C-235](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-235){.cid .st-measured}. The largest
difference is in the core, where case (b)'s $q_\mathrm{min}$ is well above case (a)'s, so
q = 1-type core modes are unlikely. Login-node equilibrium solves run one at a time: two
concurrent solves exceeded the time limit.

### Case (b) n-scan {#case-b-n-scan}

Job 1 of 5 used the case (a) job-2 protocol with three changes: the case directory, the job
group, and the health gate's reference flux on axis. It completed in 5 h 45 min
([no GMRES abort: all 8 runs reached the job time limit at t ≈ 4790 (about 4770 steps); final energies 1e-24 to 1e-20, below the 1e-15..1e-7 fit band, so no γ is fitted]{.claim}[C-236](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-236){.cid .st-measured}).

| n | t ≈ 2800 | t ≈ 3600 | t ≈ 4400 | at the end |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1–8 | −0.0005 … −0.0003 | −0.0004 … −0.0002 | −0.0003 … −0.0001 | decaying, rates approaching 0 |
| 12 | −0.00024 | −0.00012 | +0.00029 | just turned positive |
| 16 | −0.00021 | +0.00046 | +0.00173 | growing, still accelerating |
| 20 | +0.00011 | +0.00267 | +0.00287 | growing, steady over t 4000–4771 |

Local rates of ½ ln E in units of $1/\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0}$, over windows of 370 time units
([γ√(μ₀ρ₀) ≈ 0.0029, steady over t 4000–4771; flow perturbation peaks at psi_N 0.95–1]{.claim}[C-237](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-237){.cid .st-preliminary}, [at t ≈ 4400: n = 1–8 −0.0003 to −0.0001 (decaying), n = 12 +0.00029, n = 16 +0.00173 (rising)]{.claim}[C-238](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-238){.cid .st-preliminary}).

- **Growth.** Only n = 20 grows cleanly so far, at about 0.0029, roughly 15× below case
  (a)'s edge modes, in the lower-pressure state ([66.6 keV in case (a) (EQDSK pressure split by TORAX density) against 14.4 keV in case (b) (TORAX at 80 s)]{.claim}[C-239](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-239){.cid .st-measured}).
- **Location.** The growing flow perturbation of n = 20 sits at $\psi_N$ 0.95–1. The
  temperature perturbation still carries a broad, n-independent start-up component peaked at
  the axis, so the temperature-based class reads "axis" for every n. `j5_growth.py` now
  also reports `class_u`; case (a)'s classes are unchanged under it.
- **Energies.** 1e-24 to 1e-20 at the end, below the case (a) band, so no γ is fitted.

**Job 2** continues every n from its own latest time slice, with unchanged inputs. JOREK's
time slices are full restart files, written by the same routine as `jorek_restart.h5`; a
login-node restart of n = 20 resumed at t = 4771.11, step 4801.

**The grid check does not fit as planned.** Case (b)'s modes emerge from round-off only after
t ≈ 3000–4500. A 160 × 256 run repeating that from scratch, at the estimated 30–75 s per
step, needs about 40–100 h per mode, far beyond the remaining jobs. JOREK's
`jorek2_import_perturbation` needs identical grids, and the initial perturbation is
hard-coded, so seeding the doubled grid with the 80 × 128 eigenmode would need a source
patch. The options go to the owner after job 2.

### Case (b) second job {#case-b-job2}

Job 2 continued every n from its own last time slice of job 1, with Δt = 1 on the 80 × 128
grid, and ran to the time limit (t ≈ 9470–9670) with no solver abort
([the continuation job ran all eight n to its time limit (t ≈ 9470–9670) with no solver abort; n = 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8 show no measurable growth by t ≈ 9671 (under 6 decades above their minimum energy)]{.claim}[C-243](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-243){.cid .st-measured}). The window rule ("rule b", `j5_growth.py --rule b`) was fixed in the
plan before this job's data were read:
- fit ½ ln E of the total energy from 4 to 10 decades above the run's minimum, or to the end
  of the record;
- half-window and magnetic/kinetic fits must agree within 2%;
- location comes from the flow perturbation (`class_u`);
- an n that hasn't grown 6 decades is reported as "no measurable growth by t".

| n | result | γ√(μ₀ρ₀) | u peak ψ_N | γ/ω*ᵢ | fit points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 | no measurable growth by t ≈ 9671 | — | — | — | — |
| 12 | linear, edge | 0.00218 | 0.925 | 0.054 | 2669 |
| 16 | linear, edge | 0.00192 | 0.975 | 0.036 | 3425 |
| 20 | linear, edge | 0.00288 | 0.975 | 0.043 | 2403 |

([γ√(μ₀ρ₀) = 0.00218 (n = 12), 0.00192 (n = 16) and 0.00288 (n = 20), all with the flow perturbation peaked at ψ_N 0.925–0.975; fits over 2400–3400 points, half-window and magnetic/kinetic fits agreeing within 0.6%, and shifting the fit band by a decade changes γ by under 1e-4]{.claim}[C-244](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-244){.cid .st-preliminary}, [γ/ω*ᵢ = 0.054 (n = 12), 0.036 (n = 16), 0.043 (n = 20), against the EPED-like threshold 0.25; ω*ᵢ is an estimate from the profiles, not a JOREK output]{.claim}[C-245](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-245){.cid .st-preliminary}.)
- **Robustness.** The largest disagreement between half-windows, or between the magnetic and
  kinetic fits, is 0.6% (n = 16). Shifting the band by a decade either way changes γ by less
  than 1e-4.
- **Order of events.** The rule was fixed in the plan first. One look at interim output
  with the old case (a) band followed while the job ran. The rule's code was then written
  by a session that had not seen the data.

**Time-step check (job 3).** n = 12, 16 and 20 each restart twice from the same job-2 slice,
at Δt = 1 and Δt = 0.5. The slice is the first one at or after the mode's rule-b window start
(time-slice indices 7000, 6200 and 4900). The inputs are frozen with checksums, and the
comparison window and the 5% test are fixed in `j5_dt_check.py` before the run. The same
job runs the 160 × 256 axisymmetric start on the spare cores.

**Grid check.** A from-scratch doubled-grid check costs about 10–32 chained jobs
([repeating the slow emergence (4 decades only by t ≈ 4700–6900) plus a fit window on 160 × 256 means about 7000–9000 steps per mode, about 60–190 h at an estimated 30–75 s per step, so 10–32 chained jobs for the three modes run together]{.claim}[C-246](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-246){.cid .st-preliminary}). JOREK can't start the fine grid from the coarse mode in this version:
`jorek2_import_perturbation` needs identical grids, and `regrid` and `refinement` are
marked as not working. [OQ-43](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-43) asks the owner how to proceed. The recommendation is the grid
check on case (a)'s two faster pedestal modes, with case (b) reported as converged in Δt only.

### Case (b) time-step check {#case-b-dt-check}

Job 3 restarted n = 12, 16 and 20 twice from the same job-2 time slice (the first slice at or
after each mode's fit-window start), at Δt = 1 and Δt = 0.5. The inputs were frozen with
checksums. `j5_dt_check.py`, fixed before the run, fits both runs over the same window: from
100 time units after the slice to the earlier of either run's end and 10 decades above the
minimum energy.

- **Doubled grid.** The same job ran the 160 × 256 axisymmetric start on 64 spare cores:

### Case (b) grid check {#case-b-grid-check}

The owner chose the full check from round-off ([OQ-43](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-43) (b)). n = 12, 16 and 20 run again on
160 × 256. The grid is the only change; Δt = 1 and every other input are as on 80 × 128. Each
mode starts from the doubled-grid axisymmetric state of the time-step job. Six-hour jobs form
a chain, and each job restarts every mode from its own latest time slice, which carries the
energy history. Fixed before any 160 × 256 linear step, with every input frozen by checksum:
- **Comparison** (`j5_grid_check.py`). Rule b is applied to both grids unchanged. A mode
  passes decision 7 if both fits are linear, the flow perturbation peaks at the edge on both
  grids, and γ changes by at most the 5% tolerance. The 80 × 128 values recompute exactly
  from the saved runs. The 160 × 256 fit over the 80 × 128 decade band is reported but not
  gated.
- **Chain stop.** A mode needs no further job once its record reaches the top of its
  80 × 128 fit window: 9.04, 9.72 and 10.0 decades above its minimum for n = 12, 16 and 20.
  It also stops if it ends on the GMRES abort.
- **Memory gate.** The job script starts runs one at a time. It starts the next only if the
  memory left after the first-step peaks seen so far is at least 1.3 times the largest peak.

| layout (processes × threads) | cores | s per linear step | first-step peak |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 × 32, two runs per node | 64 | 15.9–16.1 | 234–235 GB |
| 2 × 64 | 128 | 11.2 | 238 GB |
| 4 × 32 | 128 | 6.1 | 270 GB |
| 80 × 128, 2 × 16 (time-step job) | 32 | 4.2 | about 54 GB |

([one linear run on the 160 × 256 grid peaks at 234–238 GB during its first step (270 GB with 4 processes × 32 threads), about four times the 80 × 128 run; two runs fit on one node]{.claim}[C-270](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-270){.cid .st-measured}, [a linear step on the 160 × 256 grid takes 6.1 s with 4 processes × 32 threads, 11.2 s with 2 × 64 and 16 s with 2 × 32 (two runs per node); on 80 × 128 it takes 4.2 s with 2 × 16]{.claim}[C-271](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-271){.cid .st-measured}.)
- In the first job the gate held n = 20 back after n = 12 and 16 had started, as designed.
  n = 20 now runs as a second chain on its own node, and a mode filter keeps each mode in one
  chain.
- From the second job on, both chains run at 4 × 32. The 4 × 32 and 8 × 16 runs used for
  timing restart from the axisymmetric state and are not part of the chain.
- About seven jobs in all are expected, against an approved envelope of 32.

## Ceilings {#ceilings}

- No growth rate passes decision 7 yet. Case (a)'s pedestal modes are converged in Δt only;
  case (b)'s three pedestal modes are converged in Δt at 80 × 128, and their grid check is
  running ([OQ-43](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-43) (b)).
- The fixed boundary at the separatrix stabilises peeling modes artificially (no vacuum
  region).
- The case (b) equilibrium is not TORAX's: q differs by up to about 14% in the core
  ([median q difference +10.7% (psi_N 0.1–0.5), +3.2% (0.5–0.9), −4.9% (0.9–0.95); q95 4.64 against 4.89, q_min 1.84 against 1.64]{.claim}[C-235](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-235){.cid .st-measured}), by construction of [OQ-40](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-40) (a).
- A doubled-grid check of slowly emerging modes costs several node-days: one 160 × 256
  linear run needs about 235 GB, so a node holds two ([one linear run on the 160 × 256 grid peaks at 234–238 GB during its first step (270 GB with 4 processes × 32 threads), about four times the 80 × 128 run; two runs fit on one node]{.claim}[C-270](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-270){.cid .st-measured}).
- The grid set-up abort under OpenMP is unexplained; it is to be reported upstream.

## Fine-grid resource disposition {#grid-budget-disposition}

An independent native-output replay preserves the unchanged comparison rule and reproduces the retained incomplete result for each selected mode ([all three selected fine-grid checks remain incomplete; the measured-cost projection exceeds the existing compute envelope and further submissions stop]{.claim}[C-291](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-291){.cid .st-preliminary}). The mode-specific restart states satisfy the existing health checks. Scheduler records and the complete chain reconcile consumed allocations; no recorded link remains active.

The resource diagnostic fits the logarithm of magnetic-plus-kinetic mode energy over several recent windows. It takes the largest positive slope, extrapolates to the original decade target, and divides the remaining simulated time by the latest link's achieved advance. Modes sharing a node are counted together; the separate mode chain adds its cost. A mode with no positive recent slope has no finite forecast. These calculations estimate cost and do not replace the frozen linear-phase fit or yield a physical growth-rate claim.

Even the optimistic finite part of the current projection exceeds the existing envelope, before assigning any cost to the mode without a forecast. Future slopes could change. This is a scenario based on retained progress, not a rigorous lower bound. The existing owner condition stops additional submissions at this point. Unused nominal allocations cannot be consumed after that gate has fired.

The fine-grid outcomes remain incomplete. The private decision package retains the exact projection, raw energy parents, healthy restart hashes, accounting and an unchanged next-link plan. A partial continuation would require an explicit owner resource and stopping-rule disposition; no physics, seeding, target or comparison tolerance is changed.
